ui.title: FarmBot Lab
ui.subtitle: Program the drone to look after the farm
ui.console.empty: What happens during the run shows up here.
help.title: How to play
help.step1: The code on the left is the orders for the drone. Each line is one order, and it follows them from top to bottom.
help.step2: Click Run. The farm starts over from scratch and the drone follows the orders.
help.step3: Watch the drone work on the farm. The console, below, tells what happened and warns you if there is a mistake.
help.step4: Change the code and click Run again. Reset clears the farm without running anything.
help.ticks: Each order takes time, measured in ticks. The meter shows how much the run spent: the fewer ticks, the better the code.
help.commands.title: Orders the drone understands
help.cmd.move: goes one cell: Dir.NORTH, Dir.EAST, Dir.SOUTH or Dir.WEST
help.cmd.plant: plants in the drone's cell: Plant.GRASS or Plant.WHEAT (wheat needs tilled soil and hay in stock)
help.cmd.harvest: harvests the plant in the drone's cell (if it is not ready yet, it is lost)
help.cmd.till: tills the drone's cell (or undoes the tilling)
help.cmd.wait: waits the given number of ticks, for example 130
help.cmd.log: writes whatever is between the parentheses to the console
help.cmd.random: gives a random number between 0 and 1
help.cmd.getPos: tells which cell the drone is in
help.cmd.getSize: tells the size of the field
help.cmd.getPlant: tells which plant is in the drone's cell
help.cmd.isReady: tells whether the plant in the drone's cell is ready to harvest
help.cmd.getTerrain: tells whether the drone's cell is grass or tilled soil
help.cmd.getStock: tells how much is in stock: Item.HAY or Item.WHEAT
help.bilingual: Every order also works in Portuguese (for example, mover instead of move).
console.started: Run started. The farm started over from scratch.
console.destroyed: The plant was harvested before it was ready and was lost. Use isReady() to know the right time.
console.bumped: The drone tried to leave the field and stayed where it was.
reject.occupied: the cell already has a plant.
reject.needs-tilled-terrain: this plant needs tilled soil. Use till() first.
reject.not-enough-hay: there is not enough hay in stock. Harvest grass to get hay.
